items.title: Chuck Lamb interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, February 7, 2023
items.q: my first experience playing with him was at it was called E-town... So we just sat there and just improvised together for about an hour.

ctx.x: Let me ask you about a couple of people that, according to your own resume, you have crossed paths with. Bela Fleck?

Forget about it. Amazing. You know that dude, we were playing, well I was doing this, my first experience playing with him was at it was called E-town which is a radio show, it’s like the “Prairie Home Companion” and it’s in Boulder. And so E-town had the © Fillius Jazz Archive -15-

Flecktones and I was playing with different people. But before we had finished all the rehearsals and stuff and the stage was dark and I went over and started playing a little bit and Bela came over with his banjo and Victor Wooten came over.
